subject: Private deployment: tenant activation & initial network sanity check-in
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Mike Jensen <mike.jensen@oncohealth.com>, procurement@oncohealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Tenant activation & initial network sanity check-in

Hi Mike —

Thanks for the call earlier. Per our intake notes, we want to run a short sanity sweep before scheduling the formal activation window next week. The goal is to validate the account-level pieces (service accounts, interconnect, routing) and confirm there are no blockers that would prevent the tenant bootstrap.

Action items I propose for this thread (short checklist):
- Confirm the list of service account emails we should provision for your environment and the permissions scope (see attached).
- Validate that OncoHealth will allow outbound egress to Redwood control-plane endpoints (redwood-api-us1.redwood.ai:443) and our telemetry ingest (telemetry.redwood.ai:443).
- Share the customer-side network topology (VPC/subnet ranges, NAT/gw public egress IPs) so we can pre-authorize routes.
- Confirm whether you plan to use a transit gateway, Direct Connect, or site-to-site VPN.

Attachments: onboarding_matrix.xlsx (worksheet with proposed service accounts + example IAM roles), network-topology-v1.pdf (requested topology placeholder).

If you can confirm the above by end-of-day Monday we can lock an activation slot for Thurs 12/3.

Thanks —
Priyom
Priyom Das
Platform Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
pri...@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0134

From: Mike Jensen <mike.jensen@oncohealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <pri...@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@oncohealth.com, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 12:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Tenant activation & initial network sanity check-in

Priyom —

Thanks for the outline. Quick answers below, and I attached the current topology export.

- Service accounts: Please provision redwood-infer-svc@oncohealth.com and redwood-ingest-svc@oncohealth.com with the minimal IAM roles you listed. We prefer scoped roles not full admin.
- Egress: We will allow outbound 443 to the domains you listed from the tenant NAT IP pool 18.204.33.128/27.
- Topology: We're on Direct Connect with a TGW in account-ops (attachment: onco-topo-20261128.json). We can also temporarily enable a site-to-site VPN if you need a quick path for the activation window.

One ask: can Redwood provide the control-plane FQDNs and a short-lived IP-range manifest so our netsec team can pre-approve? Procurement will also follow up with standard SOW questions.

—Mike
Mike Jensen
Network Engineering Manager | OncoHealth
mike.jensen@oncohealth.com | +1 415-867-2200

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Mike Jensen <mike.jensen@oncohealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:31:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Tenant activation & initial network sanity check-in

Looping in a couple of quick operational notes from our side:

- IP manifests: Attached is a short-lived IP manifest we can use for pre-approval (service-account-playbook.md contains the canonical FQDNs + ephemeral IP ranges we announce during activation). Note these are NATed addresses and we recommend whitelisting the FQDNs rather than raw IPs if your firewall can do FQDN allowlists.
- Service account permissions: We recommend granting the least-privilege roles outlined in onboarding_matrix.xlsx; for initial bootstrap, the two service accounts only need token mint and storage object read permissions.
- Activation window: If you enable temporary site-to-site VPN it speeds bootstrap validation with minimal risk — Direct Connect works too but cutover validation tends to be slower because of route propagation.

Proposed run cadence for the activation slot (estimated 90 minutes):
1) 0-15m: account credentials and SA verification
2) 15-45m: control-plane reachability, TLS handshake checks, repo/artifact pull test
3) 45-75m: model pull + inference smoke on sample traffic (restricted to test CIDR)
4) 75-90m: telemetry and logging validation, final sign-off

If that looks good we'll provision the activation-day runbook and share a short Loom for ops.

(attachment: service-account-playbook.md)

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 510-555-0199

Hi all —

Thanks for the quick confirmations. Mike, we've dropped the short-lived IP manifest and an activation runbook into the shared drive (link below). Ben — please confirm the run cadence and I'll put the 90-minute slot on the calendar for Thurs 12/3 10:00-11:30 PT.

Notes for procurement: we have a one-page SOW addendum that covers activation acceptance criteria and rollback steps; procurement@oncohealth.com, if you want it before sign-off I can send a PDF.

Drive links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bOnco-activation
Runbook: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1runbook-activation-v1

If no objections, we will:
- Provision the two service accounts with the scoped roles by EOD Tuesday
- Request OncoHealth netsec to whitelist FQDNs for the temporary window
- Share a Loom walkthrough and the activation checklist (internal ops runbook)

Cheers —
Lauren Bishop
Onboarding Lead | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0178
